questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which element of the first transition series (3d series) shows every oxidation state from +2 to +7?

solution.explanation: The number of oxidation states is greatest in or near the middle of the series, where both 4s and 3d electrons can take part in bonding. Manganese (3d⁵4s²) can use all seven of these electrons.
steps: Mn: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s² → maximum oxidation state = 2 + 5 = +7
Mn shows +2 (MnSO₄), +3, +4 (MnO₂), +6 (K₂MnO₄) and +7 (KMnO₄)
Sc shows mainly +3, Zn only +2, Cu mainly +1 and +2
solution.why_others_wrong: Sc and Zn sit at the ends of the series and show essentially one oxidation state; Cu shows only +1 and +2.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', oxidation states

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The spin-only magnetic moment of the Fe³⁺ ion in aqueous solution (Z of Fe = 26) is about:

solution.explanation: Fe³⁺ is 3d⁵. Water is a weak-field ligand, so the five electrons stay unpaired.
steps: Fe: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² → Fe³⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵
n = 5 unpaired electrons
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.90 BM is for Fe²⁺ (3d⁶, n = 4). 3.87 BM is for n = 3. 1.73 BM assumes the electrons pair up, leaving one unpaired, which does not happen with water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Because of the lanthanoid contraction, which pair of elements has almost the same atomic radius?

solution.explanation: The 4f electrons shield the nuclear charge poorly, so radii shrink steadily across the lanthanoids. This cancels the expected increase from the 4d to the 5d series, so Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are almost the same size.
steps: Going from period 5 to period 6 adds a shell, which should increase the radius
The 14 lanthanoids in between contract the radius by about the same amount
Result: 4d and 5d elements of the same group (Zr/Hf, Nb/Ta, Mo/W) have nearly equal radii
solution.why_others_wrong: Ti/Zr, Sc/Y and V/Nb are 3d/4d pairs: no lanthanoids lie between them, so the heavier element is clearly larger.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', lanthanoid contraction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In acidic solution, the permanganate ion is reduced to Mn²⁺ by gaining five electrons per ion.
Statement II: Orange dichromate solution turns yellow when its pH is raised, because dichromate changes into chromate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Oxidising action of KMnO₄ and the chromate–dichromate equilibrium
solution.explanation: In acid, MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (Mn goes from +7 to +2). Chromate (yellow) and dichromate (orange) interconvert with pH: 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O. Adding alkali removes H⁺ and shifts the equilibrium to chromate.
steps: Statement I: oxidation state of Mn changes from +7 to +2 → 5 electrons → true
Statement II: raising pH (adding OH⁻) shifts the equilibrium to yellow CrO₄²⁻ → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many moles of Fe²⁺ ions are oxidised to Fe³⁺ by 0.1 mol of K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic solution?

solution.concept: Electron balance in a dichromate titration
solution.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, so one Cr₂O₇²⁻ accepts 6 electrons. Each Fe²⁺ gives one electron.
steps: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O
Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻
So 1 mol Cr₂O₇²⁻ oxidises 6 mol Fe²⁺
0.1 mol × 6 = 0.6 mol Fe²⁺
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.3 mol counts the change of only one Cr atom (3 electrons). 0.5 mol uses the 5 electrons of permanganate. 0.1 mol assumes a 1 : 1 mole ratio.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the 3d series are correct?

(a) Sc³⁺ ions are coloured in aqueous solution.
(b) Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation because many unpaired d electrons take part in metallic bonding.
(c) Manganese shows a maximum oxidation state of +8.
(d) Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded as transition metals because their d orbitals are completely filled in the ground state and in their common oxidation state.
(e) Copper is the only 3d metal with a positive standard electrode potential E°(M²⁺/M).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Check each statement against the electronic configurations and the trends in the d-block chapter.
steps: (a) Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰: no d–d transition is possible, so it is colourless → false
(b) Unpaired d electrons strengthen metallic bonding → high atomisation enthalpies → true
(c) The highest oxidation state of Mn is +7 (in MnO₄⁻) → false
(d) Zn²⁺, Cd²⁺, Hg²⁺ are d¹⁰, so these metals are not counted as transition metals → true
(e) E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V; all other 3d metals have negative values → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (a) or (c) is wrong; (a) is the usual trap because Sc is in the 3d series but its only ion has no d electrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', general properties of the transition elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An aqueous M²⁺ ion of the 3d series has a spin-only magnetic moment of about 3.87 BM. M can be (atomic numbers: Ti 22, Mn 25, Fe 26, Co 27):

solution.concept: Working back from μ to the number of unpaired electrons
solution.explanation: μ = √[n(n + 2)] = 3.87 BM gives n = 3. Aqua complexes of M²⁺ ions are high spin, so the d count must be d³ or d⁷.
steps: Ti²⁺ 3d² → 2 unpaired (2.83 BM); Mn²⁺ 3d⁵ → 5 (5.92 BM)
Fe²⁺ 3d⁶ → 4 (4.90 BM); Co²⁺ 3d⁷ → 3 (3.87 BM)
solution.why_others_wrong: Mn²⁺ and Fe²⁺ have 5 and 4 unpaired electrons. Ti²⁺ has only 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Titrations with potassium permanganate are not carried out in the presence of hydrochloric acid.
Reason (R): Permanganate oxidises hydrochloric acid to chlorine, so part of the titrant is used up by the acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Choice of acid in permanganate titrations
solution.explanation: KMnO₄ is a strong enough oxidant to oxidise Cl⁻ to Cl₂. In HCl, some permanganate would react with the acid instead of the substance being estimated, giving a wrong (high) titre. Dilute H₂SO₄ is used instead.
steps: A is true: permanganate titrations are done in dilute H₂SO₄
R is true: 2MnO₄⁻ + 16H⁺ + 10Cl⁻ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O
R is exactly why HCl is avoided → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the aquated ion in List-I with its colour in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ti³⁺
B. Cu²⁺
C. Zn²⁺
D. Mn²⁺

List-II:
I. Colourless
II. Pink
III. Purple
IV. Blue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Colour of transition metal ions from d–d transitions
solution.explanation: A transition metal ion is coloured when it has partly filled d orbitals: light of a particular wavelength excites an electron from a lower to a higher d level, and we see the complementary colour. A d¹⁰ ion has no d–d transition.
steps: Ti³⁺ (3d¹) → purple → III
Cu²⁺ (3d⁹) → blue → IV
Zn²⁺ (3d¹⁰) → no d–d transition → colourless → I
Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) → pale pink → II
solution.why_others_wrong: A-IV, B-III swaps purple Ti³⁺ and blue Cu²⁺. C-II, D-I makes d¹⁰ Zn²⁺ coloured. A-II, D-III swaps Ti³⁺ and Mn²⁺.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', formation of coloured ions
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A sample containing 1.0 mmol of ferrous oxalate (FeC₂O₄) is dissolved in dilute H₂SO₄ and titrated with 0.02 M KMnO₄ until both Fe²⁺ and oxalate are completely oxidised. The volume of KMnO₄ used is:

solution.concept: Equivalents when one compound contains two reducing parts
solution.explanation: Permanganate oxidises Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ (1 electron) and C₂O₄²⁻ to 2CO₂ (2 electrons). So each FeC₂O₄ gives 3 electrons, and each MnO₄⁻ takes 5.
steps: Electrons given: 1.0 mmol × 3 = 3.0 mmol
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O → mmol MnO₄⁻ = 3.0/5 = 0.60 mmol
Volume = 0.60 mmol / 0.02 mmol mL⁻¹ = 30 mL
solution.shortcut: mmol × electrons must match: 0.02 × V × 5 = 1.0 × 3 → V = 30 mL.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 mL counts only Fe²⁺ (1 electron). 20 mL counts only oxalate (2 electrons). 50 mL assumes a 1 : 1 mole ratio of KMnO₄ to FeC₂O₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the f-block elements.

(a) Yb²⁺, with a 4f¹⁴ configuration, acts as a reducing agent, changing to the common +3 state.
(b) Actinoids show a smaller range of oxidation states than lanthanoids.
(c) The most common oxidation state of the lanthanoids is +3.
(d) Eu²⁺ is a strong oxidising agent.
(e) Ce⁴⁺ is a strong oxidising agent, changing to the common +3 state.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Oxidation states of lanthanoids and actinoids
solution.explanation: Lanthanoids mainly show +3; a +2 ion tends to lose an electron and a +4 ion to gain one, returning to +3. The 5f, 6d and 7s levels of actinoids are close in energy, so actinoids show many more oxidation states.
steps: (a) Yb²⁺ (4f¹⁴) readily loses an electron to become Yb³⁺ → reductant → true
(b) Actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states (uranium, for example, reaches +6) → false
(c) +3 is the characteristic oxidation state of lanthanoids → true
(d) Eu²⁺ (4f⁷) readily changes to Eu³⁺, losing an electron → it is a strong reducing agent → false
(e) Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) readily gains an electron to become Ce³⁺ → strong oxidant → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping the roles of Eu²⁺ (reductant) and Ce⁴⁺ (oxidant) is the trap behind options that include (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the lanthanoids and the actinoids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The spin-only magnetic moments (in BM) of the manganese species in K₂MnO₄ and in KMnO₄ are, respectively (Z of Mn = 25):

solution.concept: Oxidation state → d-electron count → magnetic moment
solution.explanation: In K₂MnO₄ manganese is +6; in KMnO₄ it is +7. Mn has seven valence electrons (3d⁵4s²).
steps: K₂MnO₄: 2(+1) + x + 4(−2) = 0 → x = +6 → 3d¹ → n = 1 → μ = √3 = 1.73 BM (green, paramagnetic)
KMnO₄: +1 + x − 8 = 0 → x = +7 → 3d⁰ → n = 0 → μ = 0 (diamagnetic)
solution.why_others_wrong: '0 and 1.73' swaps the two compounds. Values with 2.83 BM (n = 2) treat Mn(VI) as 3d², as if Mn had eight valence electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an ambidentate ligand?

solution.explanation: An ambidentate ligand can bind to the metal through either of two different donor atoms, but only one at a time. The nitrite ion can bind through N (nitrito-N) or through O (nitrito-O).
steps: NO₂⁻: donor atom N or O → ambidentate
en and C₂O₄²⁻ bind through two atoms at the same time → bidentate (chelating), not ambidentate
NH₃ has a single donor atom → unidentate
solution.why_others_wrong: Bidentate ligands use two donor atoms together; ambidentate ligands use one of two possible donor atoms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms (ligands)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] is:

solution.explanation: The cation is named first. In an anionic complex the metal name ends in -ate (iron → ferrate) and its oxidation state follows in Roman numerals. CN⁻ as a ligand is 'cyanido'.
steps: Charge of the complex ion: 3 K⁺ → [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻
Name: potassium hexacyanidoferrate(III)
solution.why_others_wrong: (II) gets the oxidation state wrong. 'iron' is used only for a cationic or neutral complex. The cation must come first.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An octahedral complex has the composition CoCl₃·4NH₃, and cobalt has a coordination number of 6 in it. When 0.01 mol of the complex is treated with excess AgNO₃ solution, the mass of AgCl precipitated is (molar mass of AgCl = 143.5 g mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Werner's theory: primary (ionisable) and secondary valences
solution.explanation: Coordination number 6 needs six ligands: four NH₃ and two Cl⁻. Only the remaining Cl⁻ lies outside the coordination sphere and is precipitated by Ag⁺.
steps: Formula: [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl → one ionisable Cl⁻
mol AgCl = 0.01 × 1 = 0.01 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.870 g counts two ionisable chlorides and 4.305 g counts all three, ignoring the chloride ligands bound to Co. 0.718 g halves the correct amount.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hardness of water is estimated by simple titration with Na₂EDTA, as Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ form stable complexes with EDTA.
Statement II: Chlorophyll, the pigment responsible for photosynthesis, is a coordination compound of iron.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: EDTA titrations are the standard way to estimate Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺. Chlorophyll is a magnesium complex; haemoglobin is the iron complex.
steps: Statement I: EDTA forms stable complexes with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ → true
Statement II: chlorophyll contains Mg, not Fe → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications of coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ignoring the pairing energy, the crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE) of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is:

solution.explanation: In an octahedral field each t₂g electron is stabilised by 0.4 Δo and each eg electron destabilised by 0.6 Δo. CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand, so Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) is low spin.
steps: Fe²⁺: 3d⁶; strong field (Δo > P) → t₂g⁶ eg⁰
solution.why_others_wrong: −0.4 Δo is the high-spin value (t₂g⁴ eg²), as if CN⁻ were a weak-field ligand. −2.0 Δo uses Fe³⁺ (t₂g⁵). −1.6 Δo is for t₂g⁴ (a d⁴ low-spin ion).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The total number of stereoisomers (geometrical and optical) possible for [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ is:

solution.concept: Geometrical and optical isomerism in octahedral [M(AA)₂B₂] complexes
solution.explanation: The two Cl ligands can be trans or cis. The trans form has a mirror plane, so it is optically inactive. The cis form has no mirror plane, so it exists as a pair of enantiomers.
steps: trans-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺: 1 isomer (achiral)
cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺: 2 isomers (d and l)
Total = 1 + 2 = 3
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only cis and trans and misses the optical pair. 4 wrongly gives the trans form an enantiomer too.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', isomerism in coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic, whereas [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic.
Reason (R): NH₃ is a weaker field ligand than F⁻.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Co³⁺ is 3d⁶. F⁻ is a weak-field ligand (Δo < P), so the electrons go into eg before pairing: t₂g⁴eg², four unpaired electrons. NH₃ is a stronger field ligand (Δo > P), so all six electrons pair in t₂g: diamagnetic.
steps: A: [CoF₆]³⁻ has 4 unpaired electrons, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has none → true
R: in the spectrochemical series F⁻ < H₂O < NH₃, so NH₃ is the stronger field ligand → false
solution.why_others_wrong: R reverses the spectrochemical order; the true reason is that NH₃ is the stronger field ligand.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the complex in List-I with the hybridisation of the metal in List-II.

List-I:
A. [Ni(CO)₄]
B. [CoF₆]³⁻
C. [PtCl₄]²⁻
D. [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻

List-II:
I. dsp²
II. sp³
III. d²sp³
IV. sp³d²

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Valence bond theory: hybridisation and geometry
solution.explanation: Decide the d count of the metal and whether the ligand pairs the d electrons. Strong-field ligands (CO, CN⁻) free inner d orbitals; F⁻ does not, so outer 4d orbitals are used.
steps: [Ni(CO)₄]: Ni(0), CO pairs electrons into 3d¹⁰ → 4s4p³ → sp³, tetrahedral → II
[CoF₆]³⁻: Co³⁺ 3d⁶, F⁻ weak → outer orbital sp³d², 4 unpaired → IV
[PtCl₄]²⁻: Pt²⁺ 5d⁸ → one 5d orbital emptied → dsp², square planar → I
[Fe(CN)₆]³⁻: Fe³⁺ 3d⁵, CN⁻ strong → inner orbital d²sp³, 1 unpaired → III
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes giving [CoF₆]³⁻ d²sp³ treat F⁻ as a strong-field ligand; codes giving [Ni(CO)₄] dsp² confuse it with square planar d⁸ complexes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about isomerism in coordination compounds are correct?

(a) [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ and [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ are linkage isomers.
(b) [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆] and [Cr(NH₃)₆][Co(CN)₆] are ionisation isomers.
(c) [Co(NH₃)₅(SO₄)]Br and [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ are ionisation isomers.
(d) A square planar complex of the type [MABCD] shows optical isomerism.
(e) [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ and [Cr(H₂O)₅Cl]Cl₂·H₂O are solvate (hydrate) isomers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Name each pair by what differs between the two formulas: the donor atom of one ligand, the ligands shared between a complex cation and anion, the ion inside versus outside the sphere, or water inside versus outside.
steps: (a) NO₂⁻ bound through N in one and through O in the other → linkage → true
(b) Ligands are exchanged between the cationic and anionic complexes → coordination isomers, not ionisation isomers → false
(c) SO₄²⁻ and Br⁻ swap between the coordination sphere and the counter-ion → ionisation → true
(d) A square planar complex lies in a plane, which is a mirror plane → never optically active → false
(e) Water inside versus outside the sphere → solvate (hydrate) isomers → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', isomerism in coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Equimolar aqueous solutions of the following are compared. Which one has the lowest molar conductivity?

solution.explanation: Molar conductivity rises with the number of ions a complex gives in solution. Ligands inside the square brackets do not ionise.
steps: [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ → 4 ions
[Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ → 3 ions
[Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl → 2 ions
[Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃] → non-electrolyte (no ions) → lowest conductivity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ absorbs light most strongly at 498 nm, owing to a t₂g → eg transition of its single d electron. The crystal field splitting energy Δo in kJ mol⁻¹ is about (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Δo from the absorption wavelength of a d¹ ion
solution.explanation: For a d¹ ion, the energy of the absorbed photon equals Δo (the gap between t₂g and eg). Convert the energy per ion into energy per mole.
steps: Δo ≈ 240 kJ mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 120 halves the photon energy. 24.0 comes from a power-of-ten slip in converting nm to m. 401 divides by 0.6, wrongly treating the photon energy as only the eg rise (0.6 Δo).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The spin-only magnetic moments (in BM) of [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ and [FeF₆]³⁻ are, respectively:

solution.concept: Ligand strength decides the number of unpaired electrons
solution.explanation: Both contain Fe³⁺ (3d⁵). CN⁻ pairs the d electrons (inner orbital d²sp³ complex); F⁻ does not (outer orbital sp³d² complex).
steps: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻: 3d⁵ paired as far as possible in three orbitals → 1 unpaired → √3 = 1.73 BM
[FeF₆]³⁻: 5 unpaired → √35 = 5.92 BM
solution.why_others_wrong: '5.92 and 1.73' swaps strong and weak field. '0 and 4.90' treats iron as Fe²⁺. 3.87 BM (3 unpaired) has no basis for a d⁵ ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The total number of stereoisomers (geometrical and optical together) of the octahedral ion [Co(en)(NH₃)₂Cl₂]⁺ is:

solution.explanation: The en ligand must span two cis positions. Then place the two NH₃ and the two Cl ligands in the four remaining positions and look for mirror symmetry.
steps: Isomer 1: two Cl trans to each other (NH₃ cis) → has a mirror plane → 1 isomer
Isomer 2: two NH₃ trans to each other (Cl cis) → has a mirror plane → 1 isomer
Isomer 3: both Cl cis and both NH₃ cis (each trans to an en N) → no mirror plane → a pair of enantiomers
Total = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 (3 geometrical isomers, one of them chiral)
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 counts only the geometrical isomers. 2 treats the ion like [MA₄B₂] (cis/trans only). 5 wrongly makes a second geometrical isomer chiral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a tetrahedral crystal field, the e orbitals lie higher in energy than the t₂ orbitals.
Statement II: Since Δt is only about (4/9)Δo, low-spin tetrahedral complexes are common.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Crystal field splitting in tetrahedral complexes
solution.explanation: In a tetrahedral field the splitting is inverted relative to the octahedral case: the t₂ set is higher and the e set lower. Δt ≈ (4/9)Δo is too small to force pairing, so low-spin tetrahedral complexes are rarely observed.
steps: Statement I: in a tetrahedral field t₂ is above e → false
Statement II: Δt ≈ (4/9)Δo is true, but the conclusion is the opposite: tetrahedral complexes are almost always high spin → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II starts with a true fact and draws a false conclusion; reading only its first half leads to option D.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in tetrahedral coordination entities
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: Glycerol decomposes at or below its normal boiling point. In industry it is recovered from spent-lye by:

solution.explanation: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure. Lowering the pressure lowers the boiling point, so a liquid that decomposes at its normal boiling point can be distilled without decomposing.
steps: Glycerol has a high boiling point and decomposes near it
Reducing the pressure lets it boil at a much lower temperature
This is how glycerol is separated from spent-lye in the soap industry
solution.why_others_wrong: Steam distillation needs a steam-volatile liquid immiscible with water (glycerol mixes with water). Sublimation and crystallisation are for solids.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', methods of purification
solution.final_answer: Option C: Distillation under reduced pressure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In a Carius determination, 0.20 g of an organic compound gave 0.287 g of AgCl. The percentage of chlorine in the compound is (Ag = 108, Cl = 35.5):

solution.explanation: All the chlorine of the compound ends up in AgCl. The fraction of chlorine in AgCl is 35.5/143.5.
solution.why_others_wrong: 71.0% uses 71 (Cl₂) per mole of AgCl. 47.2% divides by the atomic mass of Ag (108) instead of the molar mass of AgCl. 17.8% halves the correct value.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis (halogens)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In Dumas' method, 0.28 g of an organic compound gave 44.8 mL of nitrogen, measured at STP. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is (molar volume at STP = 22400 mL):

solution.explanation: Nitrogen of the compound is collected as N₂ gas. Convert its volume at STP to mass using 28 g of N₂ per 22400 mL.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10% uses 14 instead of 28 for a mole of N₂. 40% counts each mole of N₂ twice. 2.0% uses 224000 mL for the molar volume (a power-of-ten slip).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis (nitrogen)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about Lassaigne's test (sodium fusion extract) are correct?

(a) Nitrogen is indicated by a Prussian blue colour when the extract is boiled with FeSO₄ and then acidified with concentrated H₂SO₄.
(b) When both nitrogen and sulphur are present, sodium thiocyanate forms and gives a blood-red colour with Fe³⁺ ions.
(c) During sodium fusion, the nitrogen of the compound is converted into sodium nitrite.
(d) Before the AgNO₃ test for halogens, the extract is boiled with dilute HNO₃ to convert halide ions into free halogens.
(e) Sulphur is indicated by a violet colour with sodium nitroprusside.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Detection of N, S and halogens by sodium fusion
solution.explanation: Fusion with sodium converts covalent N, S and X into NaCN, Na₂S and NaX, which are then tested as ions.
steps: (a) NaCN + FeSO₄ → ferrocyanide; with Fe³⁺ in acid → Prussian blue → true
(b) N and S together → NaSCN → [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ blood red → true
(c) Nitrogen becomes NaCN, not NaNO₂ → false
(d) HNO₃ is used to decompose NaCN and Na₂S (which would interfere with AgNO₃), not to make free halogen → false
(e) S²⁻ + sodium nitroprusside → violet colour → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', qualitative analysis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In a Kjeldahl estimation, the ammonia evolved from 1.0 g of an organic compound was absorbed in 50 mL of 0.5 M H₂SO₄. The remaining acid needed 60 mL of 0.5 M NaOH for neutralisation. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is:

solution.explanation: The ammonia uses up part of the acid; the rest is found by titration with NaOH. H₂SO₄ is dibasic, so count millimoles of H⁺.
steps: H⁺ taken = 50 × 0.5 × 2 = 50 mmol
H⁺ left (= NaOH used) = 60 × 0.5 = 30 mmol
H⁺ used by NH₃ = 50 − 30 = 20 mmol → NH₃ = 20 mmol → N = 20 mmol = 0.28 g
solution.why_others_wrong: 70% assumes all the acid reacted with NH₃ (ignores the back titration). 42% takes the NaOH used as the NH₃. 14% treats H₂SO₄ as monobasic when finding the acid used.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', Kjeldahl's method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In thin layer chromatography, the component that is adsorbed more strongly on the stationary phase has the higher Rf value.
Reason (R): Rf = (distance moved by the substance from the base line) / (distance moved by the solvent from the base line).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A strongly adsorbed component is held back by the stationary phase and moves a shorter distance, so its Rf is smaller. R correctly defines Rf.
steps: Strong adsorption → short distance moved → low Rf → A is false
R is the definition of Rf → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A or B would need A to be true; the trap is reversing the link between adsorption and distance moved.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', chromatography
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The hybridisation of the three carbon atoms in acrylonitrile, CH₂=CH–C≡N, taken from left to right, is:

solution.concept: Hybridisation from the type of bonds at each carbon
solution.explanation: A carbon with one double bond is sp²; a carbon with a triple bond is sp; a carbon with only single bonds is sp³.
steps: CH₂= : double bond → sp²
=CH– : double bond → sp²
–C≡N : triple bond → sp

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The numbers of σ and π bonds in buta-1,3-diene, CH₂=CH–CH=CH₂, are:

solution.explanation: Every single bond is one σ bond; a double bond is one σ plus one π bond.
steps: C–H bonds: 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6 σ
C–C single bond: 1 σ
Two C=C: 2 σ + 2 π
Total: 9 σ and 2 π
solution.why_others_wrong: 6σ counts only C–H bonds. 11σ counts each double bond as two σ bonds. 4π counts each double bond as two π bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₃
B. CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)₂CHO
C. CH₂=CH–CH(CH₃)₂
D. (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CO–CH₃

List-II:
I. 3-Methylbut-1-ene
II. 4-Methylpentan-2-one
III. 2,2-Dimethylbutanal
IV. 4-Methylpentan-2-ol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: IUPAC names: longest chain containing the principal group, lowest locants
solution.explanation: Choose the longest chain that contains the principal functional group (or the double bond), number it to give that group the lowest locant, then name the substituents.
steps: A: 5-carbon chain, OH on C2, CH₃ on C4 → 4-methylpentan-2-ol → IV
B: CHO carbon is C1, two CH₃ on C2, chain of 4 → 2,2-dimethylbutanal → III
C: double bond from C1, CH₃ on C3, chain of 4 → 3-methylbut-1-ene → I
D: C=O on C2, CH₃ on C4, chain of 5 → 4-methylpentan-2-one → II
solution.why_others_wrong: A-II with D-IV swaps the alcohol and the ketone; the -ol and -one suffixes settle these two.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of organic compounds
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following can act as a nucleophile?

solution.explanation: A nucleophile has an electron pair to donate. Neutral molecules with a lone pair on N or O, such as amines and water, are nucleophiles. Cations such as NO₂⁺ and carbocations, and electron-deficient molecules such as AlCl₃, accept electron pairs.
steps: (C₂H₅)₂NH has a lone pair on N → nucleophile
NO₂⁺ and (CH₃)₃C⁺ are electron deficient → electrophiles
AlCl₃ has an incomplete octet on Al → electron-pair acceptor
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nucleophiles and electrophiles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Homolytic cleavage of a covalent bond gives carbocations.
Statement II: In heterolytic cleavage of a C–X bond, if the carbon keeps the shared pair of electrons, a carbanion is formed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In homolytic cleavage each atom takes one electron of the bond, giving free radicals. In heterolytic cleavage one atom takes both electrons: carbon becomes a carbocation if it loses the pair and a carbanion if it keeps it.
steps: Statement I: homolysis gives free radicals, not carbocations → false
Statement II: carbon with the pair → negative charge → carbanion → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', fission of a covalent bond
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many structural isomers (alcohols and ethers together) have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O?

solution.explanation: C₄H₁₀O is saturated and acyclic, so it is either an alcohol or an ether. Count each class separately.
steps: Alcohols (4): butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol
Ethers (3): 1-methoxypropane, 2-methoxypropane, ethoxyethane
Total = 7
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 counts only the alcohols. 8 adds the two enantiomers of butan-2-ol, which are stereoisomers, not structural isomers. 6 misses one isomer, usually 2-methoxypropane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the strongest acid?

solution.concept: −I effect of halogens and acid strength
solution.explanation: An electron-withdrawing group near the –COOH group spreads out the negative charge of the carboxylate ion and stabilises it. The more electronegative the halogen, the stronger its −I effect.
steps: −I effect: F > Cl > Br; CH₃ shows +I
Acid strength: FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH > CH₃COOH
solution.why_others_wrong: CH₃ is electron-releasing and makes acetic acid the weakest. Cl and Br are less electronegative than F.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', inductive effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The electromeric effect is a temporary effect.
Reason (R): The inductive effect is transmitted through σ bonds and dies down quickly as the number of intervening bonds increases.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The electromeric effect is the complete transfer of a π-electron pair of a multiple bond to one atom, which happens only when an attacking reagent is present and is undone when it is removed. R is a correct statement about a different effect (the inductive effect), so it cannot explain A.
steps: A: the electromeric effect operates only in the presence of a reagent → temporary → true
R: the inductive effect weakens rapidly along a chain → true
R describes the inductive effect, not why the electromeric effect is temporary → B
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', electronic displacements
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the pair of compounds in List-I with the type of isomerism they show in List-II.

List-I:
A. Butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol
B. Ethoxyethane and 1-methoxypropane
C. Propanal and propanone
D. Pentane and 2,2-dimethylpropane

List-II:
I. Chain isomerism
II. Position isomerism
III. Functional group isomerism
IV. Metamerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ask what differs: the skeleton (chain), the position of a group on the same skeleton (position), the functional group (functional), or the alkyl groups on either side of the same functional group (metamerism).
steps: A: OH on C1 versus C2 of the same chain → position → II
B: both ethers; C₂H₅/C₂H₅ versus CH₃/C₃H₇ around O → metamerism → IV
C: aldehyde versus ketone → functional group → III
D: straight versus branched chain → chain → I
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reactive intermediates are correct?

(a) A carbanion is an electron-deficient species.
(b) The positively charged carbon of a carbocation is sp² hybridised and has a vacant p orbital.
(c) Carbocations act as nucleophiles.
(d) Carbocation stability follows the order 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺.
(e) In a carbanion such as CH₃⁻, the carbon is sp³ hybridised and the ion is pyramidal.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure and stability of carbocations and carbanions
solution.explanation: A carbocation has six electrons around the charged carbon (electron deficient, planar, sp²). A carbanion has eight electrons including a lone pair (electron rich, sp³, pyramidal).
steps: (a) A carbanion carries an extra electron pair → electron rich → false
(b) Carbocation: three σ bonds in a plane, empty p orbital → true
(c) Carbocations accept electron pairs → electrophiles → false
(d) Alkyl groups stabilise the positive charge by +I effect and hyperconjugation → true
(e) CH₃⁻: three bond pairs + one lone pair on sp³ carbon → pyramidal → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', reactive intermediates

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many hydrogen atoms in 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃, can take part in hyperconjugation with the double bond?

solution.concept: Hyperconjugation needs C–H bonds on the carbon next to the double bond (α-hydrogens)
solution.explanation: Only C–H bonds on sp³ carbons directly attached to the C=C can overlap with its π system. The H on the double-bond carbon itself (vinylic H) does not count.
steps: sp³ carbons attached to C=C: two CH₃ groups on C2 and one CH₃ on C3
The vinylic H on C3 is excluded
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 includes the vinylic hydrogen. 6 counts only the two methyl groups on C2. 3 counts only one methyl group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which of the following reactions does a carbon atom that is sp² hybridised in the organic reactant become sp³ hybridised in the product?

options.text: Reaction of CH₃Br with aqueous KOH to give CH₃OH
Addition of HCN to CH₃CHO to give a cyanohydrin
Reaction of CH₃CH₂Br with alcoholic KOH to give CH₂=CH₂
Nitration of benzene to give nitrobenzene

solution.concept: Change of hybridisation in addition, substitution and elimination
solution.explanation: Addition to a C=O or C=C bond turns an sp² carbon into an sp³ carbon. Substitution keeps the hybridisation; elimination turns sp³ into sp².
steps: CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN: carbonyl carbon sp² → sp³ ✓
CH₃Br → CH₃OH: sp³ → sp³ (substitution)
CH₃CH₂Br → CH₂=CH₂: sp³ → sp² (elimination)
C₆H₆ → C₆H₅NO₂: ring carbons are sp² before and after (substitution)
solution.why_others_wrong: Elimination is the reverse change (sp³ → sp²); nitration passes through an sp³ intermediate but the product carbon is sp² again.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Addition of HCN to CH₃CHO to give a cyanohydrin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The total number of stereoisomers of butane-2,3-diol, CH₃–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH₃, is:

solution.concept: Stereoisomers when two chiral centres are identically substituted
solution.explanation: With n chiral centres the maximum is 2ⁿ. When the two centres carry the same four groups, the (R,S) form has a plane of symmetry and is identical to its mirror image (meso), so one isomer is lost.
steps: C2 and C3 are both chiral (H, OH, CH₃, CH(OH)CH₃)
Combinations: (R,R), (S,S), (R,S), (S,R)
(R,R) and (S,S) are enantiomers; (R,S) = (S,R) is the meso form
Total = 3
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 applies 2ⁿ without checking for a meso form. 2 counts only the optically active pair.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₂=CH–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–COOH is:

solution.concept: Numbering from the principal functional group
solution.explanation: –COOH has priority over C=C, so its carbon is C1 even though this gives the double bond a higher locant.
steps: Principal chain: 5 carbons including the COOH carbon → pentenoic acid
C1 = COOH, C2 = CH₂, C3 = CH(CH₃), C4=C5 double bond
Name: 3-methylpent-4-enoic acid
solution.why_others_wrong: 'pent-1-en-5-oic acid' numbers from the double bond, giving the principal group a higher locant. '2-methyl' puts the methyl on the wrong carbon. 'hex' counts six chain carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of compounds with functional groups

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The –NO₂ group withdraws electron density from the benzene ring, and the ortho and para positions become the most electron-deficient.
Reason (R): The –NO₂ group shows a +I effect.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The nitro group withdraws electrons by the −I effect and, more strongly, by the −R effect. The resonance structures place positive charge at the ortho and para positions, so these are the most electron-deficient.
steps: A: resonance structures of nitrobenzene show δ+ at ortho and para → true
R: –NO₂ is electron-withdrawing, i.e. −I, not +I → false
solution.why_others_wrong: A student who remembers only that −NO₂ affects ortho/para may accept R; a +I group would release electrons, the opposite of A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance effect
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The canonical (resonance) structures of a molecule can be isolated separately.
(b) Resonance structures differ only in the positions of electrons, not in the positions of atomic nuclei.
(c) The –OH group attached to a benzene ring shows a +R effect.
(d) The resonance hybrid has a lower energy than any of the contributing structures.
(e) Hyperconjugation involves delocalisation of σ electrons of a C–H bond of an alkyl group attached to an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared p orbital.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Canonical structures are imaginary limiting forms; only the hybrid exists. Lone pairs on O, N or a halogen attached to a ring are donated into it (+R).
steps: (a) Only the hybrid exists; canonical structures cannot be isolated → false
(b) Nuclei stay fixed; only electrons are moved → true
(c) A lone pair of O is delocalised into the ring → +R → true
(d) The hybrid is more stable (lower in energy) than any one structure → true
(e) This is the definition of hyperconjugation (σ–π conjugation) → true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pent-1-en-4-yne, HC≡C–CH₂–CH=CH₂, contains three sp²-hybridised carbon atoms.
Statement II: An sp hybrid orbital has 50% s character, so an sp-hybridised carbon is more electronegative than an sp² or sp³ carbon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Assign each carbon from its bonds, then use the link between s character and electronegativity.
steps: HC≡ (C5) and ≡C– (C4): sp, sp
–CH₂– (C3): sp³
–CH= (C2) and =CH₂ (C1): sp², sp²
Only two sp² carbons → Statement I false
s character: sp 50% > sp² 33% > sp³ 25%; greater s character → greater electronegativity → Statement II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Counting the CH₂ carbon next to the double bond as sp² gives three, the error Statement I invites.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which statement about the conformations of ethane is correct?

options.text: The staggered conformation has the least repulsion between C–H bond pairs and is more stable than the eclipsed form.
The eclipsed conformation is more stable because its C–H bonds are closest together.
The staggered and eclipsed forms can be separated and stored at room temperature.
In the staggered conformation, the dihedral angle between C–H bonds on adjacent carbons is 0°.

solution.concept: Conformations of ethane and torsional strain
solution.explanation: Rotation about the C–C σ bond gives conformations. In the eclipsed form the C–H bonds of the two carbons are directly behind each other and repel most; in the staggered form they are farthest apart.
steps: Staggered: dihedral angle 60°, minimum repulsion → most stable
Eclipsed: dihedral angle 0°, maximum repulsion (torsional strain)
The energy barrier is only about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, so the forms interconvert rapidly and cannot be isolated
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', conformations of ethane
solution.final_answer: Option A: The staggered conformation has the least repulsion between C–H bond pairs and is more stable than the eclipsed form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a condition for a compound to be aromatic according to Hückel's rule?

options.text: Complete delocalisation of the π electrons in the ring
Presence of (4n + 2) π electrons in the ring
Presence of at least one heteroatom in the ring

solution.explanation: A compound is aromatic if it is planar, its π electrons are completely delocalised round the ring, and the ring holds (4n + 2) π electrons (n = 0, 1, 2 …). Nothing requires a heteroatom; benzene has none.
steps: Benzene: planar, 6 π electrons (n = 1) delocalised, no heteroatom → aromatic
So a heteroatom is not a requirement
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromaticity
solution.final_answer: Option D: Presence of at least one heteroatom in the ring

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The volume of oxygen needed for the complete combustion of 2 L of propane, both gases measured at the same temperature and pressure, is:

solution.concept: Combustion of alkanes and Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes
solution.explanation: Balance the combustion equation; at the same T and P, volumes of gases are in the ratio of their moles.
steps: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
1 L propane needs 5 L O₂
2 L propane needs 10 L O₂
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 L is for 1 L of propane. 7 L uses the ratio for ethane (3.5 per litre). 6 L burns only the carbon to CO₂ and forgets the hydrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ethyne reacts with sodium metal to form sodium acetylide and hydrogen gas.
Statement II: The hydrogen atoms of ethene are more acidic than those of ethyne.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A hydrogen on a triply bonded carbon is attached to an sp carbon (50% s character). That carbon holds the bonding pair closer, so the H is released as H⁺ more easily than from sp² (ethene) or sp³ (ethane) carbons.
steps: Statement I: HC≡CH + Na → HC≡C⁻Na⁺ + ½H₂ → true
Statement II: acidity order is ethyne > ethene > ethane → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', acidic character of alkynes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene followed by treatment with zinc and water gives:

solution.concept: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond into two C=O groups
solution.explanation: Cut the double bond and put =O on each carbon that was part of it.
steps: (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃
(CH₃)₂C= → (CH₃)₂C=O, propanone
=CH–CH₃ → CH₃CHO, ethanal
solution.why_others_wrong: Butanone + methanal comes from 2-methylbut-1-ene. Two propanal come from hex-3-ene. 2-Methylpropanal + methanal comes from 3-methylbut-1-ene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', ozonolysis of alkenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many open-chain alkenes have the molecular formula C₅H₁₀, counting geometrical (cis/trans) isomers separately?

solution.concept: Structural and geometrical isomerism in alkenes
solution.explanation: List the structural isomers first; then check which have two different groups on each double-bond carbon.
steps: Straight chain: pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene
Branched: 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene → 5 structural isomers
Only pent-2-ene has two different groups on both sp² carbons → cis and trans
Total = 5 + 1 = 6
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 ignores geometrical isomerism. 7 wrongly gives 2-methylbut-2-ene cis/trans forms, but one of its double-bond carbons carries two CH₃ groups.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Benzene readily undergoes addition reactions like alkenes.
Reason (R): Benzene is stabilised by the delocalisation of its six π electrons (resonance).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Because the π electrons are delocalised, benzene is unusually stable. It prefers electrophilic substitution, which keeps the aromatic ring, to addition, which would destroy it. Addition happens only under drastic conditions.
steps: A: benzene does not decolourise bromine water or react like an alkene → false
R: resonance (delocalisation) stabilises benzene → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', structure of benzene and resonance
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with its main organic product in List-II.

List-I:
A. Propyne + H₂O (Hg²⁺, dilute H₂SO₄, 333 K)
B. Ethyne + H₂ (Pd on charcoal partly deactivated with quinoline)
C. Ethene + Br₂ (in CCl₄)
D. Ethyne passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K

List-II:
I. Benzene
II. Propanone
III. 1,2-Dibromoethane
IV. Ethene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Identify each reaction: hydration of an alkyne (Markovnikov), partial hydrogenation, halogen addition and cyclic polymerisation.
steps: A: CH₃C≡CH + H₂O → enol → CH₃COCH₃ (propanone) → II
B: Lindlar-type catalyst stops reduction at the alkene → CH₂=CH₂ → IV
C: Br₂ adds across C=C → BrCH₂CH₂Br → III
D: three ethyne molecules cyclise → benzene → I
solution.why_others_wrong: A gives propanone, not propanal, because H₂O adds by Markovnikov's rule; full hydrogenation to ethane would need an active catalyst.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: chemical properties
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the preparation and properties of alkanes are correct?

(a) Heating sodium propanoate with soda lime gives ethane.
(b) Alkenes add hydrogen in the presence of finely divided Pt, Pd or Ni to give alkanes.
(c) 2,2-Dimethylpropane (neopentane) has a higher boiling point than n-pentane.
(d) Alkyl halides (other than fluorides) are reduced by zinc and dilute HCl to alkanes.
(e) Chlorination of methane in diffused sunlight gives only chloromethane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Recall the standard methods (decarboxylation, hydrogenation, reduction of alkyl halides) and the effect of branching on boiling point.
steps: (a) Decarboxylation removes one carbon: C₂H₅COONa + NaOH → C₂H₆ + Na₂CO₃ → true
(b) Catalytic hydrogenation of alkenes → alkanes → true
(c) Branching makes the molecule more compact (smaller surface area), lowering the boiling point → false
(d) R–X + H₂ (Zn, H⁺) → R–H → true
(e) Free-radical chlorination continues to CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄ → mixture → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: preparation and properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which substituent on a benzene ring deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution and yet directs the incoming group to the ortho and para positions?

solution.explanation: Halogens withdraw electrons strongly by the −I effect, which deactivates the ring. Their lone pairs donate by the +R effect, which builds up electron density at the ortho and para positions, so attack goes there.
steps: –Cl: −I > +R → deactivating; +R decides orientation → o/p directing
–CH₃ and –OCH₃: activating, o/p directing
–NO₂: deactivating, meta directing
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', directive influence of a functional group in monosubstituted benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An open-chain alkene of formula C₆H₁₂ gives only one carbonyl compound on ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O). The mass of this carbonyl compound obtained from 8.4 g of the alkene, assuming complete reaction, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: A single product means the double bond sits in the middle of a symmetrical molecule, so each molecule of alkene gives two identical C₃ carbonyl molecules. The two possible alkenes, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (→ propanone) and hex-3-ene (→ propanal), both give a product of molar mass 58 g mol⁻¹.
steps: Moles of alkene = 8.4/84 = 0.1 mol
Each mole gives 2 mol of C₃H₆O (M = 58)
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.8 g forgets that each alkene gives two carbonyl molecules. 8.8 g takes the product to be ethanal (M = 44). 8.4 g assumes the mass stays the same.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many structurally different monochloro products can be formed by free-radical chlorination of 2-methylbutane?

solution.concept: Equivalent hydrogens decide the number of monosubstitution products
solution.explanation: Each set of equivalent hydrogens gives one monochloro product. In CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃, the two methyl groups on C2 are equivalent.
steps: C1 and the methyl branch (equivalent) → 1-chloro-2-methylbutane
C2 → 2-chloro-2-methylbutane
C3 → 2-chloro-3-methylbutane
C4 → 1-chloro-3-methylbutane
Total = 4 structural isomers
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 treats the two methyls on C2 as different. 6 also counts the enantiomers of the two chiral products, which the question excludes. 3 misses one set of hydrogens.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Addition of HBr to propene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide gives 1-bromopropane as the main product.
Reason (R): The peroxide effect is observed equally in the addition of HCl and HI to alkenes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: With peroxide, HBr adds by a free-radical chain, giving the anti-Markovnikov product. With HCl the H–Cl bond is too strong to be split by the radicals, and with HI the iodine radicals combine to I₂ instead of adding, so no peroxide effect is seen.
steps: A: anti-Markovnikov addition → CH₃CH₂CH₂Br → true
R: the peroxide effect is seen only with HBr → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', anti-Markovnikov addition (peroxide effect)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about benzene and its reactions are correct?

(a) Nitrobenzene undergoes Friedel–Crafts alkylation easily.
(b) All six C–C bonds in benzene have the same length, 139 pm.
(c) Benzene reacts with Cl₂ in the presence of UV light to give chlorobenzene.
(d) Friedel–Crafts alkylation of benzene with CH₃Cl needs anhydrous AlCl₃.
(e) Toluene undergoes nitration faster than benzene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure and electrophilic substitution of benzene
solution.explanation: Delocalisation makes the C–C bonds equal. Electron-withdrawing groups deactivate the ring; electron-releasing groups activate it. In UV light benzene adds chlorine instead of being substituted.
steps: (a) –NO₂ strongly deactivates the ring; nitrobenzene does not undergo Friedel–Crafts reactions → false
(b) Bond length 139 pm lies between C–C (154 pm) and C=C (133 pm) → true
(c) UV light → addition → C₆H₆Cl₆ (benzene hexachloride) → false
(d) AlCl₃ generates the electrophile CH₃⁺ → true
(e) –CH₃ is activating (+I, hyperconjugation) → faster nitration → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following has the longest carbon–halogen bond?

solution.concept: Size of the halogen and C–X bond length
solution.explanation: Bond length increases with the size of the halogen atom: F < Cl < Br < I.
steps: C–F < C–Cl < C–Br < C–I
Iodine is the largest atom → C–I is the longest bond (about 214 pm)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nature of the C–X bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The reaction R–Cl + NaI → R–I + NaCl, carried out in dry acetone, is called:

solution.explanation: Alkyl iodides are made from alkyl chlorides or bromides with NaI in dry acetone. NaCl (or NaBr) is insoluble in dry acetone and precipitates, which drives the reaction forward.
steps: Exchange of Cl/Br for I using NaI in dry acetone → Finkelstein reaction
Swarts reaction makes alkyl fluorides (AgF, Hg₂F₂)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', halogen exchange

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: DDT is readily metabolised by animals, so it does not accumulate in their fatty tissues.
Statement II: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in the presence of light to phosgene, so it is stored in closed, dark coloured bottles filled to the top.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Environmental and storage aspects of polyhalogen compounds
solution.explanation: DDT is not metabolised rapidly; it is stored in fatty tissues and its concentration builds up along food chains. Chloroform forms the poisonous gas phosgene (COCl₂) in air and light, so air and light are kept out.
steps: Statement I: DDT accumulates in fatty tissue → false
Statement II: 2CHCl₃ + O₂ → 2COCl₂ + 2HCl (light) → storage in full, dark bottles → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following alkyl bromides undergoes SN1 hydrolysis fastest?

solution.concept: Carbocation stability controls the SN1 rate
solution.explanation: The slow step of SN1 is ionisation to a carbocation. The more stable the carbocation, the faster the reaction.
steps: Carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺
(CH₃)₃CBr gives the tertiary (CH₃)₃C⁺ → fastest SN1
solution.why_others_wrong: CH₃Br reacts fastest by SN2, which is the opposite order; the question asks about SN1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 10.9 g of bromoethane (molar mass 109 g mol⁻¹) is converted completely into ethylmagnesium bromide, which is then treated with excess water. The volume of gas formed at STP is (molar volume = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Grignard reagents react with water to give alkanes
solution.explanation: C₂H₅Br + Mg → C₂H₅MgBr; C₂H₅MgBr + H₂O → C₂H₆ + Mg(OH)Br. One mole of bromoethane gives one mole of ethane.
steps: Moles of C₂H₅Br = 10.9/109 = 0.1 mol
Ethane formed = 0.1 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.12 L assumes two ethyl groups join (as in the Wurtz reaction). 4.48 L doubles the moles. 22.4 L takes one whole mole.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reaction with metals (Grignard reagents)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane by the SN1 mechanism gives a racemic mixture.
Reason (R): The carbocation intermediate is planar, so the nucleophile attacks it from either face with equal probability.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In SN1 the C–Br bond breaks first, giving a planar sp² carbocation. Attack from the two faces gives the two enantiomers in equal amounts.
steps: A: SN1 → racemisation → true
R: planar carbocation, attack from both sides → true
R is the reason for A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with its name in List-II.

List-I:
A. 2CH₃CH₂Br + 2Na (dry ether) → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ + 2NaBr
B. 2C₆H₅Cl + 2Na (dry ether) → C₆H₅–C₆H₅ + 2NaCl
C. C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na (dry ether) → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl
D. CH₃Br + AgF → CH₃F + AgBr

List-II:
I. Swarts reaction
II. Fittig reaction
III. Wurtz–Fittig reaction
IV. Wurtz reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Named reactions of alkyl and aryl halides
solution.explanation: With sodium in dry ether: two alkyl halides → Wurtz; two aryl halides → Fittig; one of each → Wurtz–Fittig. Exchange with a metallic fluoride → Swarts.
steps: A: alkyl + alkyl → Wurtz → IV
B: aryl + aryl → Fittig → II
C: aryl + alkyl → Wurtz–Fittig → III
D: AgF → alkyl fluoride → Swarts → I
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reactions of haloalkanes and haloarenes
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 2-Bromobutane is heated with alcoholic KOH. Counting geometrical isomers separately, how many different alkenes can be formed?

solution.explanation: A β-hydrogen can be removed from C1 or from C3. Removing it from C3 gives but-2-ene, which exists as cis and trans isomers.
steps: β-H on C1 → but-1-ene
β-H on C3 → but-2-ene → cis and trans
Total = 3 alkenes (but-2-ene is the main product, by Saytzeff's rule)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 ignores cis/trans isomerism of but-2-ene. 1 gives only the Saytzeff product.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about nucleophilic substitution are correct?

(a) An SN2 reaction proceeds with inversion of configuration.
(b) The rate of an SN1 reaction depends on the concentrations of both the alkyl halide and the nucleophile.
(c) Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution, partly because resonance gives the C–X bond partial double bond character.
(d) An –NO₂ group at the ortho or para position to the halogen increases the reactivity of a haloarene towards nucleophilic substitution.
(e) Allylic and benzylic halides are highly reactive towards SN1 because their carbocations are stabilised by resonance.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: SN1, SN2 and the reactivity of haloarenes
solution.explanation: SN2 is one step with backside attack; SN1 has a slow ionisation step that involves only the substrate.
steps: (a) Backside attack → Walden inversion → true
(b) SN1 is first order: rate = k[R–X] → false
(c) Lone pair of X delocalised into the ring → stronger, shorter C–X bond → true
(d) –NO₂ at o/p stabilises the negatively charged intermediate by resonance → true
(e) Allyl and benzyl cations are resonance-stabilised → fast SN1 → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major organic product formed when 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is heated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol is:

solution.explanation: A tertiary alkyl halide is too crowded for SN2 attack. Ethoxide is a strong base, so it removes a β-hydrogen and elimination dominates.
steps: (CH₃)₃C–Br + C₂H₅O⁻ → (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ + C₂H₅OH + Br⁻
Tertiary substrate + strong base → elimination is the main pathway
solution.why_others_wrong: The ether would form by substitution, which is minor for a tertiary halide with a strong base (Williamson synthesis uses a primary halide for this reason). The alcohol needs water as the nucleophile. 2-Methylpropane would need reduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination versus substitution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following alcohols gives turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl + anhydrous ZnCl₂) at room temperature?

solution.explanation: The alkyl chloride formed is insoluble and makes the solution turbid. Tertiary alcohols react at once because they form a stable tertiary carbocation; primary alcohols do not react at room temperature.
steps: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol, (CH₃)₃C–OH, is tertiary → immediate turbidity
Butan-2-ol is secondary → turbidity after some minutes
Butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol are primary → no turbidity at room temperature
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reaction with hydrogen halides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Phenol is heated with chloroform and aqueous NaOH, and the product is acidified. The main product is:

solution.explanation: With CHCl₃ and alkali, a –CHO group is introduced at the ortho position of phenol (via a –CHCl₂ intermediate). Acidification gives 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.
steps: C₆H₅OH + CHCl₃ + NaOH → o-substituted –CHCl₂ intermediate → hydrolysed to –CHO
Acidification → salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
solution.why_others_wrong: Salicylic acid comes from Kolbe's reaction (sodium phenoxide + CO₂), not from chloroform.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', Reimer–Tiemann reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Williamson's synthesis of ethers is the reaction of:

options.text: two molecules of an alcohol with concentrated H₂SO₄
an alkene with water in the presence of acid
an aldehyde with an alcohol in the presence of dry HCl
an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide

solution.explanation: An alkoxide ion is a strong nucleophile; it displaces the halide from an alkyl halide by SN2: R–X + R′–O⁻Na⁺ → R–O–R′ + NaX. Both symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers can be made.
steps: Example: CH₃Br + C₂H₅ONa → CH₃–O–C₂H₅ + NaBr
solution.why_others_wrong: Heating an alcohol with concentrated H₂SO₄ is dehydration (another ether method, not Williamson's). Alkene + water gives an alcohol; aldehyde + alcohol gives an acetal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of ethers
solution.final_answer: Option D: an alkyl halide with a sodium alkoxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The volume of 0.1 M NaOH needed to neutralise 0.6 g of ethanoic acid (molar mass 60 g mol⁻¹) is:

solution.explanation: CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O, a 1 : 1 reaction.
steps: Moles of acid = 0.6/60 = 0.01 mol
Moles of NaOH = 0.01 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 mL slips a factor of ten. 50 mL and 200 mL treat ethanoic acid as needing half or twice the NaOH (it has only one acidic H).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ketones reduce Tollens' reagent and give a silver mirror.
Statement II: In Fehling's test, the aldehyde is reduced to a primary alcohol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both tests depend on the easy oxidation of aldehydes. The aldehyde is oxidised to the carboxylate anion; Ag⁺ is reduced to silver (Tollens'), and Cu²⁺ to red-brown Cu₂O (Fehling's). Ketones are not oxidised by these mild reagents.
steps: Statement I: ketones generally do not respond to Tollens' reagent → false
Statement II: the aldehyde is oxidised (not reduced); Cu²⁺ is the species reduced → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', oxidation (Tollens' and Fehling's tests)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 3.1 g of ethane-1,2-diol (molar mass 62 g mol⁻¹) reacts completely with excess sodium. The volume of hydrogen evolved at STP is (molar volume = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Reaction of alcohols with active metals
solution.explanation: Each –OH group gives ½ H₂ with sodium. Ethane-1,2-diol has two –OH groups, so one mole of the diol gives one mole of H₂.
steps: HOCH₂CH₂OH + 2Na → NaOCH₂CH₂ONa + H₂
Moles of diol = 3.1/62 = 0.05 mol → H₂ = 0.05 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.56 L counts only one –OH group. 2.24 L gives a whole H₂ per –OH group. 0.28 L does both halvings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the strongest acid?

solution.concept: Acidity of phenols and substituent effects
solution.explanation: Phenoxide is stabilised by resonance, so phenol is far more acidic than ethanol. An electron-withdrawing –NO₂ group at the para position delocalises the negative charge further and increases acidity; an electron-releasing –CH₃ group decreases it.
steps: pKa: ethanol 15.9 > p-cresol 10.2 > phenol 10.0 > p-nitrophenol 7.1
Lowest pKa → strongest acid → p-nitrophenol
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Anisole (methoxybenzene) reacts with HI to give phenol and methyl iodide, not iodobenzene and methanol.
Reason (R): The O–C(aryl) bond has partial double bond character because the aryl carbon is sp² hybridised and the oxygen lone pair is delocalised into the ring, so this bond is not cleaved.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Cleavage of alkyl aryl ethers by HI
solution.explanation: HI protonates the ether oxygen; I⁻ then attacks the methyl carbon (SN2). The aryl–oxygen bond is stronger, so it stays intact and phenol is formed.
steps: A: C₆H₅OCH₃ + HI → C₆H₅OH + CH₃I → true
R: the C₆H₅–O bond is stronger (sp² carbon, partial double bond) → true
R is the reason the methyl–oxygen bond breaks instead → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', cleavage of the C–O bond in ethers
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the named reaction in List-I with its reagent in List-II.

List-I:
A. Rosenmund reduction
B. Stephen reaction
C. Etard reaction
D. Clemmensen reduction

List-II:
I. CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂, then H₃O⁺
II. Zn–Hg / concentrated HCl
III. H₂, Pd–BaSO₄
IV. SnCl₂ + HCl, then H₃O⁺

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Preparation and reduction of carbonyl compounds
solution.explanation: Three of these make aldehydes (from an acyl chloride, a nitrile and toluene); Clemmensen reduction turns a C=O group into CH₂.
steps: Rosenmund: RCOCl + H₂ over Pd–BaSO₄ → RCHO → III
Stephen: RCN + SnCl₂/HCl → imine → hydrolysis → RCHO → IV
Etard: toluene + chromyl chloride → chromium complex → benzaldehyde → I
Clemmensen: >C=O → >CH₂ with zinc amalgam and conc. HCl → II
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of aldehydes and ketones
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about carboxylic acids are correct?

(a) Methanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid.
(b) Carboxylic acids are weaker acids than phenol.
(c) Carboxylic acids boil at higher temperatures than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular mass, because of extensive hydrogen bonding.
(d) The C=O group of carboxylic acids shows the usual nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes and ketones.
(e) Carboxylic acids liberate CO₂ from sodium hydrogencarbonate solution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Physical and chemical properties of carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by two equivalent resonance structures, which makes carboxylic acids stronger than phenol and stronger than carbonic acid. The same resonance reduces the electrophilic character of the carbonyl carbon.
steps: (a) CH₃ (+I) destabilises the anion; HCOOH (pKa 3.75) > CH₃COOH (pKa 4.76) → true
(b) Carboxylic acids (pKa about 4–5) are stronger than phenol (pKa 10) → false
(c) Hydrogen-bonded dimers persist even in the vapour → high boiling points → true
(d) Resonance in –COOH removes the typical aldehyde/ketone reactions of C=O → false
(e) RCOOH + NaHCO₃ → RCOONa + H₂O + CO₂ (effervescence) → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?

solution.concept: Cannizzaro reaction needs an aldehyde without α-hydrogen
solution.explanation: Aldehydes with no α-hydrogen undergo self oxidation–reduction with concentrated alkali: one molecule is reduced to an alcohol and another oxidised to a carboxylate salt. Those with α-hydrogen undergo aldol condensation instead.
steps: C₆H₅CHO: the CHO is attached to a ring carbon with no H → no α-H → Cannizzaro
2C₆H₅CHO + conc. NaOH → C₆H₅CH₂OH + C₆H₅COONa
CH₃CHO, CH₃CH₂CHO and CH₃COCH₃ have α-H → aldol reactions
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', Cannizzaro reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 0.88 g of ethanal (molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹) is completely oxidised by Tollens' reagent. The mass of silver deposited is (Ag = 108):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the silver mirror test
